description: The bar chart illustrates the distribution of narrative roles across different bias categories, comparing the proportions of "Hero", "Victim", and "Villain" roles. The horizontal axis lists four categories: "Left bias", "Left center bias", "source", and "Right bias", while the vertical axis represents the proportion, ranging from 0.0 to 1.0 with a linear scale and tick labels at intervals of 0.2. Each category is represented by a grouped bar, with "Hero" in dark blue, "Victim" in brown, and "Villain" in light blue. The "Villain" bars consistently reach the top of the chart at approximately 1.0 across all categories, while the "Hero" bars range from approximately 0.28 to 0.45, with the highest value in "Left center bias" and "source" at around 0.45 and 0.44 respectively, and the lowest in "Right bias" at around 0.28. The "Victim" bars vary between approximately 0.39 and 0.54, with the highest value in "Left center bias" at around 0.54 and the lowest in "Right bias" at around 0.39. The bars are grouped by category, with no stacking or sorting applied, and no visual emphasis is placed on any particular bar.
